description:
Bring the canonical BCH generator and parity-check materialization into conformance with the approved matrix contract: row $i$ of the generator matrix is the systematic encoding of message basis vector $i$ in the default user layout, and the parity-check matrix is a full-rank matrix in that same layout.

## Background

The reference materialization writes the polynomial-form generator (row $i$ is the coefficient vector of $x^i g(x)$) and a parity-check matrix built from the reversed quotient $(x^n - 1)/g(x)$, both in internal coordinate order, so the canonical code reports `is_systematic() == false`. The approved code-trait contract fixes the generator matrix in the user layout with row $i$ equal to the encoding of message basis vector $i$; the GLDPC component consumer reads $G = [\,I_k \mid P\,]$ directly, and the generator-matrix materialization workload of the benchmark contract is defined on that systematic form. For a cyclic code the systematic form is cheap to derive: parity row $i$ is the coefficient vector of $x^{r+i} \bmod g(x)$ with $r = n - k$, and $H = [\,-P^{\mathsf T} \mid I_r\,]$ is a full-row-rank check matrix satisfying $G H^{\mathsf T} = 0$.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: For every canonical BCH code, packed binary and field-generic, `generator_matrix_into` writes the $k \times n$ matrix whose row $i$ equals the codeword the default-layout systematic encoder produces for message basis vector $i$, so the first $k$ columns form the identity and `is_systematic()` reports true.
- [hard] REQ-02: `parity_check_matrix_into` writes a full-row-rank $(n - k) \times n$ matrix in the same user layout with $G H^{\mathsf T} = 0$; the module's tests witness both properties over $\mathrm{GF}(2)$, $\mathrm{GF}(p)$, and $\mathrm{GF}(p^r)$ fixtures, including the full-space and zero-dimensional boundary codes.
- [hard] REQ-03: The caller-buffer, allocating, and explicit-cache access paths keep their typed shape-error and caching contracts, and the module documentation states the user-layout contract in place of the polynomial-form description.

## Notes

Polynomial-form matrices may remain as test oracles for row membership in the code; they are not a public materialization. Optimizing the materialization for the benchmark workload dimensions is separate work that builds on this corrected reference.
title: Canonical BCH matrices use the systematic user layout
